summary.headline: Sell practical workflow automation to small UK businesses before building software.
summary.best_opportunity: Productized workflow automation for one small-business niche
summary.why_now: The latest official 2025 estimate counts 5.7 million UK private-sector businesses, including 5.64 million small businesses; this shows market breadth, not verified demand for automation.

top_opportunities.name: Niche workflow automation service
top_opportunities.description: Implement a measurable admin automation such as enquiry triage, quote follow-up or appointment reminders for one niche.
top_opportunities.why_now: A paid pilot validates a concrete productivity outcome without a software build; official business counts show a broad prospect base, not willingness to buy.
top_opportunities.buyer: Owner-managed trades and small professional or appointment-based service firms
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£600; existing tools and direct outreach keep spend low.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Potentially 1–3 weeks through direct outreach; unvalidated estimate.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly monitoring, support and incremental improvements.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong software engineering fit; solo and part-time deliverable.
risks: Trust, privacy and data handling may block adoption.
Unbounded integration support can erode margins.
top_opportunities.verdict: Best first test: sell a fixed-scope paid pilot before standardising.

top_opportunities.name: Local website care and lead conversion retainer
top_opportunities.description: Maintain and improve small business websites, enquiry forms, booking flows and conversion tracking.
top_opportunities.why_now: Tangible, familiar service can be sold to firms with broken or outdated lead flows.
top_opportunities.buyer: Local trades and small service businesses
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong web engineering fit and part-time compatible.
risks: Unclear scope can turn retainers into unlimited redesign work.
top_opportunities.verdict: Viable add-on or fallback; sell a specific outcome, not generic redesign.

top_opportunities.name: Missed-enquiry recovery for appointment firms
top_opportunities.description: Set up enquiry acknowledgement, booking links and follow-up with human handoff.
top_opportunities.why_now: Ties the service to potentially lost sales; local willingness to pay needs validation.
top_opportunities.buyer: Independent clinics, salons, garages and home-service firms
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly service and usage fee with defined limits.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good integration fit; requires onboarding and support.
risks: Consent, privacy and messaging-provider rules require care.
Buyers may already use booking software or withhold lead data.
top_opportunities.verdict: Pilot with one firm and measure response times or bookings before scaling.

top_opportunities.name: Niche local lead-generation site
top_opportunities.description: Build a specialist local directory and sell qualified enquiries to a few providers.
top_opportunities.why_now: Low-cost to launch, but organic traffic and monetisation are uncertain and slower than service sales.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Uncertain and likely slower; traffic and buyers must be established.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly listing or lead fees if demand is demonstrated.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good technical fit; requires ongoing sales and content.
risks: Search rankings can take months and are not guaranteed.
Lead quality disputes and search-platform dependence.
top_opportunities.verdict: Pre-sell provider interest before investing in content or build-out.

top_opportunities.name: Vertical micro-SaaS for repetitive admin
top_opportunities.description: Turn a repeated workflow found through paid service work into a narrow subscription tool.
top_opportunities.why_now: UK business counts are large, but no evidence here establishes a specific unmet software need; discovery must come first.
top_opportunities.buyer: A narrow group of small firms sharing a frequent administrative problem
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Uncertain and slower; pre-sell or find design partners first.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Subscription only if repeated use and retention are proven.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Excellent engineering fit; distribution remains the key challenge.
risks: Building before willingness to pay is proven wastes time and budget.
Existing tools and acquisition costs may make the product uneconomic.
top_opportunities.verdict: Second-stage choice, not the strongest immediate-cash option.

best_pick.name: Niche workflow automation service
best_pick.why_it_wins: Low upfront cost, strong engineering fit and a service-led path to near-term paid validation; recurring support may follow successful delivery.
validation_plan: Interview 10 owners in one reachable niche about a repeated workflow, current tools and actual cost.
Offer a fixed-scope paid pilot to three prospects; continue only if at least one pays and the result is measurable.
best_pick.first_offer: £250–£500 fixed-scope workflow audit and pilot, with explicit data handling and support limits.
best_pick.mvp: One automation using the client's existing tools, with human review, basic logging, failure alerts and documented handover.
customer_types: Local trades businesses handling quote requests
best_pick.do_today: Choose one niche, write a one-page outcome-based offer and contact 10 local owners to arrange discovery calls.
